stories.headline: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
stories.title: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
stories.summary: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were accused of breaking into an unauthorised protest venue in Delhi.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Two leaders of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) have been freed from jail a week after they were arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka walked out of Tihar jail hours after a magistrate ordered their release.
They had been detained by police and jailed after they crossed barricades and climbed over the locked gate at Jantar Mantar.
The men, who denied wrongdoing, have been calling on India's chief election commissioner to resign.
Critics accuse the commission of manipulating voter rolls to benefit India's governing party, charges the commission rejects.
A special executive magistrate court in Delhi, passed their release order, legal news website Bar and Bench reported.
After bail was granted, Das told reporters from a police van: "Truth alone triumphs.
Das and Ranka are key leaders of the CJP, which began as an internet joke in May after India's top judge compared unemployed young people to "cockroaches".
The CJP is not a registered political party, but a collective which began by mobilising thousands of young people to protest over leaked exam papers.
By July it had emerged as a major force.
A march towards parliament that month ended in clashes with police, drawing wider attention to the movement and increasing pressure on the government.

stories.headline: Ladakh High Court bench begins regular hearings
stories.title: Ladakh High Court bench begins regular hearings
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 21: A historic chapter in Indian judicial history unfolded on Wednesday when Chief Justice of the High Court of J&K and Ladakh, Dr Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar presided over the first regular division bench at Leh. The newly established Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh located at a breath-taking height of over 11,500 feet above sea level, began regular hearing of the cases from today. The day began with the hearing by the Division Bench in which the Chief Justice heard the matters through virtual mode while Justice Sanjay Parihar was present physically at the Ladakh Bench. After the conclusion of the hearing of five listed Division Bench matters, Justice Sanjay Parihar sat singly and dealt with as many as 60 matters listed before the single bench. Today’s proceedings made use of technology to facilitate a sort of hybrid hearing with the Chief Justice hearing through Virtual Mode and Justice Sanjay Parihar doing physical hearing. Justice Parihar said that the identification of the 65 cases that were listed today reflects the initial effort to organise and facilitate the hearing of matters concerning litigants from Ladakh. He added that the successful commencement of regular judicial hearings today by the Chief Justice in such a high-altitude location is a landmark achievement in the country’s judicial infrastructure and commitment to ensuring that geographical barriers do not become obstacles to justice. The establishment of the Ladakh Bench is a significant step in strengthening the reach of constitutional institutions to remote and geographically challenging regions of the country. Earlier, litigants from Leh, Kargil and other far-flung areas of Ladakh would undertake lengthy journeys to Srinagar or Jammu for proceedings before the High Court. The commencement of hearings here is also encouraging for the legal fraternity of Ladakh including advocates. It may be mentioned that the Ladakh Bench of J& K High court was formally inaugurated by the Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kanton October 18, 2026, at Melongthang, Leh. stories.headline: PM Modi has failed ‘abysmally’ on Manipur, says Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge
stories.title: PM Modi has failed ‘abysmally’ on Manipur, says Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi what has happened to the Peace Committee which was announced by home minister Amit Shah in June 2023 and what action has been taken on the Supreme Court-appointed Justice Gita Mittal Committee’s recommendations. He also asked what concrete measures have been taken to restore peace, protect citizens and address the continuing security challenges in the sensitive border state.
